question: What is the main goal of safe motherhood initiatives?

options.A: To minimize the total cost of obstetric medications
options.B: To ensure all births occur strictly inside tertiary hospitals
options.C: To reduce preventable maternal and newborn deaths
options.D: To completely eliminate pregnancy for high-risk women

explanation: You've got this! Safe motherhood is all about keeping both mum and baby safe and healthy by stopping complications before they get out of hand.

question: Why do nurse-midwives treat every pregnancy as a condition that needs careful monitoring?

options.A: Because it is an inherently pathological state that always causes injury
options.B: Because traditional birth attendants cannot manage normal deliveries
options.C: Because government regulations mandate strict hospital confinement
options.D: Because normal physiological processes can carry unpredictable risks

explanation: Even when a mum is glowing and healthy, things can change quickly. Staying watchful helps us catch any sudden surprises early!

question: Which global region currently has the highest number of maternal deaths?
explanation: As future Nigerian nurses, knowing our local context is key. Sub-Saharan Africa bears the heaviest load of maternal mortality, making our work so important.

question: In rural Nigeria, what is a major indirect reason why mothers sometimes sadly lose their lives before reaching the hospital?

options.A: Delays in reaching a healthcare facility due to poor transport
options.B: Routine use of sterile delivery kits
options.C: Early booking for antenatal care services

explanation: Bad roads and lack of vehicles mean transport delays are a massive hurdle. Getting mums to the clinic on time can literally save a life.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the core pillars of safe motherhood?
explanation: Easy pick! The real pillars are family planning, antenatal care, safe delivery care, and postnatal care.

question: Why is family planning considered a key pillar of safe motherhood?

options.A: It helps women space pregnancies to protect their physical health
options.B: It eliminates the need for any laboratory tests during pregnancy
options.C: It completely stops women from experiencing menopause
options.D: It guarantees that every baby born will be a male child

explanation: Giving mum's body time to rest and rebuild strength between babies means a healthier mother and a safer next pregnancy!

question: When is a new mother at the highest risk for postpartum complications?

options.A: During the third trimester of pregnancy
options.B: Six months after the baby is weaned
options.C: Within the first forty-eight hours after delivery
options.D: At the onset of true labor contractions

explanation: The first 48 hours after birth are critical. This is when heavy bleeding (hemorrhage) is most likely to happen, so close monitoring is a must.

question: What is the main reason a midwife uses a partograph while a woman is in labor?

options.A: To monitor the progress of labor and detect early signs of complications
options.B: To calculate the total financial cost of the hospital stay
options.C: To measure the mother's daily nutritional calorie intake
options.D: To schedule the exact date for the child's immunization

explanation: Think of the partograph as your trusty labor map! It helps you spot if labor is dragging or if the baby is stressed, long before it becomes an emergency.

question: Which of these is a serious pregnancy danger sign that a mum must report right away?

options.C: Light swelling of the feet at the end of the day

explanation: A pounding headache and blurry eyes are huge red flags for preeclampsia. Catching this early prevents dangerous seizures!

question: What is your very first nursing action if a patient starts bleeding heavily right after birth?

options.A: Massage the uterus and call for emergency assistance
options.B: Wait for laboratory results before taking any action
options.C: Send the patient home to rest in bed
options.D: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward

explanation: Act fast! Massaging the uterus makes it clamp down and stop the bleeding, while shouting for help brings your team running.

question: What is a heartbreaking result of unwanted pregnancies in places where safe care isn't available?

options.B: Automatic enrollment in advanced academic scholarships
options.C: Immediate maternal immunity against infectious diseases
options.D: Unsafe abortions leading to severe infection and bleeding

explanation: When women lack access to safe options, they often resort to dangerous procedures that cause terrible injuries and loss of life.

question: How does family planning directly help safe motherhood efforts?

options.A: By eliminating all natural causes of infertility
options.B: By helping women space pregnancies to protect their physical recovery
options.C: By ensuring women have children as rapidly as possible
options.D: By replacing the need for antenatal clinic attendance

explanation: Spacing kids gives mum's body a well-deserved break to build back her blood levels and strength before the next journey.

question: Why is it smart to involve traditional birth attendants (TBAs) in community safe motherhood programs?

options.A: To train them to recognize danger signs and refer women promptly
options.B: To grant them full authority to perform major surgeries
options.C: To eliminate the need for any modern medical clinics
options.D: To replace licensed nurses in major teaching hospitals

explanation: Many rural women trust TBAs. Training TBAs to spot trouble early means they can send mums to the hospital before it's too late.

question: Why is getting male partners involved in community safe motherhood programs so important in Nigeria?

options.A: They are solely responsible for performing postnatal physical examinations
options.B: They should be excluded from all prenatal health decisions
options.C: They act as primary birth attendants during complicated deliveries
options.D: They control household resources and support decisions to seek timely care

explanation: In many of our communities, men hold the purse strings and make transport decisions. Getting dads on board means transport and hospital fees get sorted faster!

question: What is a core duty of a nurse-midwife in promoting safe motherhood?

options.C: Providing respectful maternity care and screening during antenatal visits
options.D: Discouraging women from visiting modern hospitals

explanation: As a nurse-midwife, you are a frontline hero! You screen mums, teach them what to expect, and always treat them with love and dignity.

question: Why do modern hospitals emphasize respectful maternity care?

options.A: It guarantees that the baby will be born without any medical issues
options.B: It reduces the cost of building new maternity wards
options.C: It encourages women to choose facility delivery instead of staying home
options.D: It replaces the need for any medications during labor

explanation: Nobody wants to visit a harsh nurse! When women feel welcomed and valued in the clinic, they are happy to come back for safe deliveries.
